issue_context.title: Add --profiling flag to kubelet
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:

The control plane components have a `--profiling` flag that controls `/debug/pprof/*` and `/debug/flags/v` being enabled or disabled. Kubelet has both these endpoints, but it doesn't allow them to be independently disabled from all other debugging endpoints that support `kubectl {exec,logs,portforward}`.

**Why is this needed**:

Administrators who don't want to solely rely on RBAC roles for debug endpoints should be able to disable remote profiling and log level setting. 

See Also:
#64601
#63777

/sig node
/kind feature
/area kubelet
comments:
/sig auth

Can you elaborate on the justification?
> Administrators who don't want to solely rely on RBAC roles for debug endpoints should be able to disable remote profiling and log level setting.

Why doesn't the administrator want to solely rely on RBAC? Is it because it's hard to block access to someone with cluster-admin privileges? Would a custom authorizer that denied access to this path cover this use case (along with finer-grained authorization, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83465)? Or is this more of a defense-in-depth thing, where it's preferable to just cut out the attack surface completely?
Yes, this is about defense-in-depth, particularly in our case (Fargate) where the customer doesn't manage the kubelet or compute.
OK, that makes sense. I'm convinced this (and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/87252) would be useful.

> Yes, this is about defense-in-depth, particularly in our case (Fargate) where the customer doesn't manage the kubelet or compute.

@micahhausler In this case (and #87252), why do you not just prevent these via a deny authorizer in front of RBAC?

After sig-auth discussion, decided to defer to sig-node on this one.
/remove-sig auth

@SaranBalaji90 Sorry for not capturing your question / request in detail earlier at SIG Node. Could you please elaborate a little bit more here or follow up through slack? Thanks!

np @dchen1107 thanks for following up. This issue is created to add flag like `enableProfilingHandler` to configure both `/debug/pprof/*` and `/debug/flags/v`.

But I'm wondering if we need separate flags to configure these endpoints. For eg `enableProfilingHandler` for `/debug/pprof/*` and `enableDebugFlagsHandler` for `/debug/flags/v`.

This will make sure `enableProfilingHandler` doesn't control logging configuration flag `/debug/flags/v`

But looks like we enable both the endpoints as part of `--profiling` flag for CP components though https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/63777/files#r209802914

@SaranBalaji90 Thanks for the updates. Like what we discussed and agreed at previous SIG Node, introducing a separate flag to enable profiling is reasonable. 

To answer your above question on another separate flag to configure /debug/flags/v, I personally prefer to separate them for the cleanness. I don't have a strong opinion on this particular one. @derekwaynecarr
@SaranBalaji90 +1 to a dedicated flags for each variant of profiling.

review_comments: nit: Would be nice to say "profiling is disabled" when enableProfiling is false and debuggingHandler is enabled. Can you also add a unit test for this change.
